specification.problem: Sparse Hamiltonian simulation: approximate e^{-iHt} for a d-sparse Hamiltonian H with max entry magnitude ||H||_max to error epsilon, by combining quantum-walk steps with Bessel-function coefficients (Jacobi-Anger expansion), giving query complexity near-linear in tau = d t ||H||_max and logarithmic in 1/epsilon.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Background-level reconstruction of the Bessel-function linear-combination idea: a quantum walk operator W whose eigenphases are arcsin(lambda/(d||H||_max)) for eigenvalues lambda of H, and the Jacobi-Anger truncated expansion of e^{-i tau sin(theta)}. Excluded: the explicit walk construction, the LCU/oblivious amplitude amplification circuit, error analysis, gate-count accounting, and the lower-bound proof. No tiny circuit instance is given.

symbols.meaning: magnitude of largest entry of H
product of evolution time, sparsity and max entry magnitude
Bessel function of the first kind of order n
truncation order of the Bessel series

equations.label: Parameter definition
equations.description: Product of evolution time, sparsity and largest entry magnitude, as described in the abstract.
equations.abstract_quote: the product $\tau$ of the evolution time, the sparsity, and the magnitude of the largest entry of the Hamiltonian
equations.justification: Directly describes tau as a product of three named quantities; the symbolic form is the inference.
assumptions: d denotes sparsity and ||H||_max the largest entry magnitude

equations.label: Jacobi-Anger expansion
equations.description: Expansion of a phase in a Bessel series; with sin(theta)=lambda/(d||H||_max)-type walk eigenphases it yields e^{-iHt} as a linear combination of walk powers.
equations.justification: Standard identity; the abstract only mentions coefficients given by Bessel functions, not this exact form.
assumptions: Used as the likely mechanism, not verified against the paper

equations.label: Walk eigenphase relation (assumed)
equations.description: Typical Szegedy-style quantum walk spectrum for a Hamiltonian with normalization d||H||_max, with sin(theta)=lambda/(d||H||_max).
equations.justification: Standard form for Hamiltonian-simulation quantum walks; the paper's exact construction is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Walk built from a sparse-access oracle with normalization d||H||_max
Eigenvectors mu_pm are in the invariant subspace

equations.label: Truncated linear combination of walk powers
equations.description: Approximation of the evolution by a Bessel-weighted combination of walk steps, which is an approximation and not an exact equality; the truncation order K is a typical scaling not stated in the abstract.
equations.justification: Proposed from the Bessel-coefficient description; sign and phase corrections for the +/- branches are omitted.
assumptions: Sign and phase handling between branches omitted
Truncation scaling taken from general knowledge of Bessel decay

equations.label: Claimed complexity form
equations.description: Near-linear in tau, logarithmic in 1/epsilon, with a claimed lower bound showing no sublinear dependence on tau.
equations.abstract_quote: is logarithmic in the inverse error, and nearly linear in the product $\tau$
equations.justification: Qualitative scaling is stated; the precise polylog factors are not.

specification.initial_state: Arbitrary system state |psi> with ancillas in |0>; the specific state is not given.

steps.description: Define tau and choose truncation order K to meet error epsilon.
Build the quantum walk W whose spectrum encodes arcsin of the scaled eigenvalues of H using sparse-access queries.
Prepare control amplitudes proportional to the Bessel coefficients J_n(tau) and apply the controlled powers of W as a linear combination (LCU).
Boost success probability, for example via amplitude amplification, and compare cost scaling with the claimed result.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical computation of Bessel coefficients and choice of K; details are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: The method is assumed to be the Jacobi-Anger Bessel expansion over a quantum walk, which is background rather than paper-sourced
No explicit small instance is chosen
Normalization and sign conventions are not verified
